about: Next word: what AI is and how ChatGPT and Claude work. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.

lines.text: Every word ChatGPT has ever written to you was a guess.
One word at a time.
So how does guessing sound this smart?
First, it never sees words. It sees tokens.
Little chunks of text, and each one becomes a number.
Then it plays one game, over and over. Guess what comes next.
The cat sat on the... mat? Probably. The moon? Almost never.
Pick a word, stick it on the end, and guess again. That's the whole trick.
But where do those odds come from? Reading. A ridiculous amount of reading.
Trillions of words. Hide the next one, make a guess, check the answer.
Wrong? Nudge billions of tiny dials, just a little. Then do it again.
And here's the weird part. To guess well, it has to learn what words mean.
King, minus man, plus woman, lands right next to queen.
It also looks back at everything before, to work out what goes with what.
Here, it figures out that it means the trophy.
Out of the box, it just rambles.
So people rate its answers, and it learns to be helpful.
Do that at a huge scale, and you get ChatGPT. Or Claude.
But it's still guessing. When it doesn't know, it can sound sure and be wrong.
So it's not magic. It's the best next-word guesser ever built.
